evals.prompt: Create a nightly schedule lane that runs secrets-hygiene and license-headers, commit-by-commit, at 3am.
evals.expected_output: Following the schedule engine's `schedule-apply <root> <lane> --cron <cron> --member <id> [--member <id> ...] --evidence <range|commits> [--budget N]` contract (kit/assets/packs/lib/schedulelib.py): the skill resolves the two member tokens against `.governance/packs/*/*/directives/*/directive.yaml` (bare ids `secrets-hygiene` and `license-headers` each match exactly one installed directive here), confirms both are schedule-eligible (both carry an explicit `triggers:` list that includes `schedule` — `secrets-hygiene` is `[pre-commit, schedule]`, `license-headers` is `[schedule]` with `hook: none`), and calls `packverb.py schedule-apply <root> nightly --cron "0 3 * * *" --member governance-kit/core/secrets-hygiene --member governance-kit/core/license-headers --evidence commits`. This writes `.github/workflows/governance-schedule-nightly.yml` from `kit/assets/governance-schedule.template.yml`, appends the workflow's relative path to `.governance/install.yaml`'s `install_assets_seeded` list, and refreshes the `managed_digests` block. The report names the lane, the cron, the two resolved member ids, and the generated workflow path.
assertions: The skill resolved both `secrets-hygiene` and `license-headers` against the installed directives under `.governance/packs/governance-kit/core/directives/` before calling the engine, rather than passing the bare prompt words straight through blind

The skill confirmed both members are schedule-eligible: `secrets-hygiene` via its `directive.yaml` `triggers: [pre-commit, schedule]`, `license-headers` via `triggers: [schedule]` (with `hook: none` — it has no commit-time hook at all)

The skill invoked the schedule engine (`packverb.py schedule-apply` or the equivalent `governance schedule create` verb) with `--cron "0 3 * * *"`, two `--member` flags naming `governance-kit/core/secrets-hygiene` and `governance-kit/core/license-headers`, and `--evidence commits`
`.github/workflows/governance-schedule-nightly.yml` was created

The generated workflow contains `cron: "0 3 * * *"` under `on: schedule:`, and its `run.sh --scheduled` invocation line includes `--evidence commits` and both member ids space-joined (`governance-kit/core/secrets-hygiene governance-kit/core/license-headers`)
`.governance/install.yaml`'s `install_assets_seeded` list gained the entry `.github/workflows/governance-schedule-nightly.yml`
No other file in the repo (no `check.sh`, no `directive.yaml`, no `packs.lock` entry) was modified — creating a schedule lane is purely additive over the already-installed directives
The report names the lane (`nightly`), the cron, the resolved member ids, and the generated workflow path

evals.prompt: Set up a nightly schedule lane at 3am covering secrets-hygiene and naming-convention, commit-by-commit evidence. If something's not eligible, fix it and retry rather than giving up.
evals.expected_output: First attempt: the skill calls `schedule-apply <root> nightly --cron "0 3 * * *" --member governance-kit/core/secrets-hygiene --member acme/local/naming-convention --evidence commits`, which the engine refuses (`result: "refused"`, nonzero exit) because `naming-convention`'s effective triggers are `[pre-commit]` only — it has no `triggers:` entry in `directive.yaml`, so it derives to just its `hook:` value, and `schedule` is not in it. The refusal message names the ineligible directive and its two remediation options (add `schedule` to its `directive.yaml` `triggers:`, or add a `.governance/conf/acme/local/naming-convention.conf` overlay with a `TRIGGERS=` row that includes `schedule`). The skill then writes the overlay `.governance/conf/acme/local/naming-convention.conf` containing `TRIGGERS=pre-commit,schedule` (preserving `naming-convention`'s existing `pre-commit` hook trigger, not just adding `schedule` alone), and retries the identical `schedule-apply` call, which now succeeds and writes the workflow file.
assertions: The first `schedule-apply` invocation (or `governance schedule create`) named both `governance-kit/core/secrets-hygiene` and `acme/local/naming-convention` as members
That first attempt was refused (nonzero exit / `result: "refused"`) and produced no workflow file — `.github/workflows/governance-schedule-nightly.yml` does not exist after it

The refusal explicitly names `naming-convention` (or its full id `acme/local/naming-convention`) as the ineligible member and states its effective triggers are `[pre-commit]`, not including `schedule`
The skill did not silently drop the ineligible member and apply a partial lane over just `secrets-hygiene` — it treated the refusal as blocking, not as a reason to narrow scope without saying so
The skill created the overlay file `.governance/conf/acme/local/naming-convention.conf` with a `TRIGGERS=` row that includes `schedule`

The overlay's `TRIGGERS=` row preserves `naming-convention`'s original `pre-commit` hook trigger (e.g. `TRIGGERS=pre-commit,schedule`) rather than replacing it with `schedule` alone and silently disabling its pre-commit enforcement
The skill retried the same `schedule-apply` call after writing the overlay, and this second attempt succeeded
`.github/workflows/governance-schedule-nightly.yml` now exists and its `run.sh --scheduled` line names both `governance-kit/core/secrets-hygiene` and `acme/local/naming-convention`
`.governance/install.yaml`'s `install_assets_seeded` list gained the workflow path only after the second, successful attempt
The report is honest about the two-step path: it names the initial refusal and the overlay fix, not just the final success

evals.prompt: Remove the nightly schedule lane, we don't need it anymore.
evals.expected_output: Following `schedule-remove <root> <lane>`: the skill calls `packverb.py schedule-remove <root> nightly`, which deletes `.github/workflows/governance-schedule-nightly.yml`, removes the matching `.github/workflows/governance-schedule-nightly.yml` row from `.governance/install.yaml`'s `install_assets_seeded` list, and refreshes the `managed_digests` block (dropping the workflow's entry). No installed directive, `directive.yaml`, or `packs.lock` entry is touched — removing a lane only ever affects the generated workflow file and the install manifest's bookkeeping of it.
assertions: The skill called `packverb.py schedule-remove <root> nightly` (or the equivalent `governance schedule remove nightly` verb) rather than deleting the workflow file by hand
`.github/workflows/governance-schedule-nightly.yml` no longer exists after the operation
`.governance/install.yaml`'s `install_assets_seeded` list no longer contains `.github/workflows/governance-schedule-nightly.yml`
`.governance/install.yaml`'s `managed_digests` block no longer has an entry for the removed workflow file

No installed directive under `.governance/packs/` was modified, and `.governance/packs.lock` is unchanged — a lane removal does not uninstall or disable any directive, it only removes the generated schedule workflow
The report names the removed lane and the deleted workflow path
